Alternative solutions provided by implementing organizations

During 2025, significant progress was made in advancing the rights and inclusion of women with disabilities through advocacy, direct engagement with government departments, and awareness initiatives.Through a state-level event, advocacy efforts were successfully undertaken with the Divisional Commissioner, Chief Medical Officer, and Social Welfare Officer, leading to concrete action on facilitating disability certificates and pension benefits for persons with disabilities.Women with disabilities took proactive steps by directly approaching the concerned departments to demand essential support such as wheelchairs, pensions, and other entitlements.Additionally, these women held meaningful discussions with their caregivers on issues related to sexuality, bodily autonomy, and rights protection. This process helped sensitize caregivers, transforming them into supportive allies committed to promoting dignity, inclusion, and empowerment for persons with disabilities in their families and communities.A request was made to the state government to ensure that the specific needs of women and girls with disabilities (WGWDs) are included in all policies related to women’s safety and the prevention of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV).“Safe Space Groups” led by young women were established in communities, where regular discussions are held on gender equality, identification of violence, and its prevention. Suggestions emerging from these groups have been shared with local administration, such as ensuring the representation of young women in community monitoring committees.At the state level, training programs are being organized to strengthen the role of district, block, and Panchayat-level representatives in preventing child marriage and to ensure their accountability. The organization was given the opportunity to develop the gender module and serve as a trainer for these sessions, and this issue was included in the training agenda.

National, state level, and local level advocacy initiatives

CREA consortium partners have reported 59 collective advocacy initiatives. Diverse women leaders undertook the following collective advocacy related work. Conducted 15 panchayat level advocacy on the issue of domestic voilence, conducted quarterly outreach and advocacy meeting with N0n state duty bearers on the issue of abortion. Also conducted quarterly outreach and advocacy meeting with state duty bearers to raise Issues related to women and women's safety. Two interface meetings between Block / Police Officials on safety of women and health and safety issues and one district level workshop at Sarikela- kharsawa, disability and leadership issues. At panchayat level nine advocacy initiatives were undertaken in participation of the elected women representatives, frontline workers, self-help group members on the issue of GBVH and SRHR services. As a result the agenda on improved health services for women has been added to the panchayat level plan(GPDP)Other advocacy initiatives include advocy at block level officials for voter cards for PWDs, dialogue with police thana officials for accessible police services for adolescent girls. Demand was rained for providing shelter home at one stop centre. Meetings were conducted with district officials for transgender rights Lobbying of women leaders and institutional workers was done at Panchayat, Block, District and State. 12 advocacy meetings with various Panchayat officials done to enrourage EWRs participation, registration of voter IDs for structurally excluded persons and registration of disabled persons. Four block level advocacy initiatives regarding safe abortion MTP law for young girls so that abortion can be done easily. Five district level advocacy on issues of free distribution of sanitary pads and domestic violence case . Advocacy with the media for the use of respectful language regarding sexuality and disability in their societySDRC: YWLs and WWDs participated in state level Menstrual Health Policy advocacy, conducted dvocacy on Menstrual Health nationally , as part of the advocacy letter sent to Health Ministry. Also organised workshop with Swasthya Sangini of South 24 Parganas & explained need of inclusion of women with disabilities.CREA: At national level CREA carried out two advocacy initiatives; 1) Draft recommendations were shared with the Ministry of Health and Family welfare, Government of India who was inviting Public comments on the National Draft Policy on Menstrual Hygiene, 2) during the 16days campaign joint statement and recommendations with all WGG partners to three state – UP Bihar and Jharkhand to different stakeholders about our stand on GBV and political participation of young girls and women with disabilities Secondly, there has been a mismatch in target. The target mentioned on AIDSTREAM is 96, where as as per the consortium partners the target is 48 for the year 2023.
National, state level, and local level advocacy initiatives

In the year 2024 WGG India has advocated collectively with strategic partners to strengthen the functioning of One stop crisis Centre and make it more inclusive and disability friendly support service to the survivors of the SGBV. To push the agenda we have conducted a study together in 4 states and continuously having dialogue with the concern departments.Several women courageously raised their voices against domestic violence and took independent steps to confront and stop the abuse happening within their homes.Women approached the One Stop Center and gave formal statements against their husbands, demonstrating increased awareness about institutional support systems and confidence to seek justice.More than 20 adolescent girls successfully prevented their forced marriages, showing strong resistance against social pressure and asserting their right to make their own life choices.Young girls took a bold stand by exercising their right to choice in same-sex relationships, despite facing opposition from their families—reflecting growing awareness of individual rights and gender diversity.5 women with disabilities proactively coordinated with the Health Department to access sexual and reproductive health services, marking a positive shift toward inclusion and recognition of their health needs.
